ABOUT ME:
Computer Engineering student specializing in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Data Science through a dual-degree between the Université de Technologie de Compiègne (UTC, France) and PUCPR (Brazil).

My focus is building high-reliability intelligent systems where advanced ML models meet strict physical and edge computing constraints. At 18, I founded and ran my own apparel brand, gaining hands-on discipline in inventory management, supplier negotiations, unit economics, and operational resource allocation. At Packform and Irrigate, I turned this practical mindset into robust engineering: automating complex enterprise workflows in Python and developing C/C++ firmware on ESP32 microcontrollers for high-reliability embedded systems and end-to-end automation.

ARTICLES_TEXT: Peer-reviewed research and academic publications advancing Artificial Intelligence for structural health monitoring and industrial reliability.
ARTICLE_COBEM_TITLE: Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network for Structural Damage Prediction
ARTICLE_COBEM_DESC: Peer-reviewed paper accepted at COBEM 2025. Evaluates TabPFN for structural health monitoring (SHM), achieving 99.18% accuracy without hyperparameter tuning.
ARTICLE_COBEM_LONG_DESC:
Publication: COBEM 2025 — 28th International Congress of Mechanical Engineering.
Authors: Iago Rhudá Ramos et al.
Key Result: 99.18% accuracy on structural damage classification without any hyperparameter tuning, outperforming traditional machine learning baselines.
Summary: Investigated the frontier Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) foundation model on real-world structural vibration sensor data. TabPFN achieved state-of-the-art diagnostic accuracy with near-instant inference speed, demonstrating immense practical promise for mission-critical structural health monitoring in civil and aerospace structures.
ARTICLE_PIBIC_TITLE: Wind Turbine Blade Crack Detection via PCA & Logistic Regression
ARTICLE_PIBIC_DESC: PUCPR undergraduate research supervised by Prof. Dr. Helon Vicente Hultmann Ayala, achieving 92% predictive accuracy on wind turbine blade structural cracks.
ARTICLE_PIBIC_LONG_DESC:
Institution: Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Paraná (PUCPR).
Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Helon Vicente Hultmann Ayala.
Key Result: 92% predictive accuracy in early crack trend classification.
Summary: Applied Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for sensor dimensionality reduction combined with regularized Logistic Regression. Proved that low-frequency acoustic and vibration signatures can identify blade structural fatigue well before visible surface rupture, drastically reducing wind farm maintenance downtime. Available on request.
